title: Entropy-aware SLO & Error Budget Rebalancing Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook describes an entropy-aware approach to rebalancing SLO allocations and error budgets across multi-tenant inference services. It defines triggered conditions, an automated control loop, manual escalation steps, auditing requirements, and a safe rollout plan. The goal is to keep customer-facing SLOs intact while using capacity signals and statistical entropy metrics to proactively reallocate headroom and error budget credits when workload characteristics shift unexpectedly.

Background and motivation

As inference workloads diversify (chat, embeddings, reranking, long-form generation) we observe frequent shifts in per-tenant latency distributions, tail behavior, and token-distribution variance. Traditional static error budget partitions and per-service SLOs can either waste capacity (if partitions are conservative) or allow cascading SLO burn (if partitions are rigid). We introduce an entropy metric (distributional unpredictability) to detect when historical assumptions break and to trigger either an automated rebalance or a human-led containment.

Definitions

- SLO: service-level objective (e.g., p95 latency <= 120ms, availability >= 99.95%).
- Error budget: permitted percentage of SLO violations in a rolling window (e.g., 0.05% per 30d).
- Entropy (H): a statistical measure of distributional spread for latency or token-length distributions. Higher H indicates greater unpredictability and risk of unexpected tail events.
- Rebalance window: time interval during which budgets may be reallocated (default = 1h).
- Quarantine: temporary conservative mode applied to a tenant/service to prevent further SLO burn.

When to consider rebalancing (trigger conditions)

Automated pipeline monitors these signals and proposes or executes rebalances when multiple conditions are met within a 1h window:

1) Entropy spike: H(latency|service) rises > 30% vs. 30d rolling baseline.
2) Error-budget acceleration: burn rate over last 6h > 3x expected burn.
3) Capacity pressure: cluster free GPU headroom < 12% for > 10m.
4) Correlated anomalies: > 4 tenants show concurrent p99 regressions or timeouts.

All four => automated rebalance candidate. Any two + manual approval => operator intervention recommended.

Automated rebalance workflow (control loop)

Overview: a lightweight controller (rebalance-controller) runs in the control plane with these responsibilities:

- Continuously evaluate triggers and compute a risk score per tenant/service.
- Propose candidate reallocations of error-budget-credit and temporary headroom tokens.
- If risk score > 0.85 and capacity pressure exists, execute conservative rebalances limited by governance thresholds.
- Emit audit events for every decision and start a 30m cooldown after execution.

Step-by-step automated flow:

1) Detect: telemetry ingestion pipeline (Prometheus → pipeline service) computes H and burn rates.
2) Score: rebalance-controller computes risk_score = weighted(H_delta, burn_accel, headroom_deficit, correlated_tenants).
3) Simulate: controller runs a quick forward-simulation for 3 candidate reallocations and scores predicted SLO impact.

- If simulation predicts all critical SLOs preserved and risk_score > 0.85, controller applies:
  - shift up to 15% of flexible headroom from low-risk tenants to high-risk ones, and/or
  - grant temporary throttled priority tokens (max 10% of cluster IO slots) for 20 minutes.

4) Audit + notify: write decision to audit-log (immutable), create a PagerDuty incident with severity P3, and notify owners in Slack #sre-rebalances.

5) Cooldown: no further automatic actions for 30 minutes unless manual override.

Manual intervention and containment procedure

If automated simulation fails or the proposal would likely breach critical contractual SLOs, follow this manual sequence:

1) Triage (within 10m): on-call SRE inspects the following dashboards: SLO-summary, entropy-timeseries, capacity-heatmap, tenant-error-budget-ledger.
2) Contain (within 15m): apply quarantine to the most errant tenant(s) identified by risk_score, limiting burst tokens and forcing quality-preserving fallbacks:
  - disable large-context long-run requests for quarantined tenant;
  - redirect heavy embedding batches to deferred queue;
  - reduce model size variant for non-critical routes.
3) Stabilize (within 45m): if containment reduces headroom pressure and H returns below threshold, run a measured partial rebalance under supervision.
4) Escalate (if >2h or increasing): open an incident review using the Incident Review Standards (see References) and assign an incident lead.

Decision matrix (quick reference)

| Observed condition | Immediate action | Max reallocation allowed | Notify | Escalation threshold |
|--------------------|------------------|--------------------------|--------|---------------------|
| H rise 30–50% | Automated proposal (no execute) | n/a | #sre-rebalances | Manual approve if persists 30m |
| H rise >50% + burn accel | Automated exec (conservative) | 15% headroom, 10% tokens | PagerDuty P3 + Slack | Manual if SLO risk >0.2 |
| Capacity <5% | Mandatory containment | Quarantine top 3 tenants | PagerDuty P2 | Incident lead within 30m |
| Multi-region correlated | Route failover & canary rollback | 0 | Oncall + Product | Full incident review |

Telemetry and queries (examples)

- Entropy (approx) computed from latency histogram buckets (PromQL):
  increase(histogram_entropy_sum{job=\"inference\"}[30m]) / increase(histogram_entropy_count{job=\"inference\"}[30m])

- Error budget burn rate (6h):
  (errors{service=~\".*\"}[6h] / total_requests{service=~\".*\"}[6h]) / SLO_target_error_rate

- Headroom fractional availability:
  sum(available_gpu_slots) / sum(total_gpu_slots)

Policy and configuration example (YAML)

# rebalance-policy.yaml (example snippet)
# All numeric values are governed by central policy and must be reviewed before change.
thresholds:
  entropy_delta_pct: 30
  burn_accel_multiplier: 3
  min_headroom_pct: 12
actions:
  max_headroom_shift_pct: 15
  max_token_priority_pct: 10
  quarantine_duration_mins: 40
governance:
  max_automated_actions_per_window: 3
  auto_cooldown_mins: 30
  require_manual_approval_for_contractual_slos: true

Rollout and testing plan

1) Canary (week 0–2): enable rebalance-controller in a single region, synthetic tenants only. Verify telemetry and audit events.
2) Scoped expansion (week 3–6): enable for non-enterprise tenants in region-us-east-1 behind feature flag. Monitor for false positives and unexpected throttles.
3) Enterprise opt-in (week 7–10): invite a small set of enterprise customers for opt-in testing and provide rollback SLA.
4) Global enable (week 11+): full enablement with continuous monitoring and a 2-week rollback window.

Testing matrix (examples):
- Chaos test: simulate a 4x entropy spike for a tenant and validate automatic containment executes within 10m.
- Load test: reduce cluster headroom to 8% and verify quarantines are applied as specified.
- Regression test: ensure no critical contractual SLO is breached during automated rebalances.

Audit and evidence retention

- All controller actions MUST be written to the immutable audit-log with these fields: timestamp, controller_version, decision_id, affected_tenants, pre-state_summary, post-state_summary, simulation_score, operator_override (if any).
- Retention: audit-log entries preserved for 3 years. Short-term replication to hot-store for 90 days to support immediate forensic work.
- Evidence package for incident review should include: telemetry snapshot (raw histograms), controller simulation input/outputs, decision timeline, and chat/comm notifications.

Operational tooling integrations

- rebalance-controller (service): core control loop, exposes /decisions and /simulate endpoints.
- audit-store (service): append-only store for decisions.
- sko-dashboard (Grafana): combined SLO, entropy, and capacity heatmap.
- ork-runbook-bot (Slack): runbook automation that can apply approved manual steps and capture operator rationale.

Runbook: quick steps for oncall

1) Acknowledge PagerDuty P3 / Slack @channel.
2) Open SLO-summary & entropy heatmap; identify top 3 tenants by risk_score.
3) If automated action executed, review audit-entry and confirm post-state metrics moving in right direction.
4) If not executed and risk high, apply containment (quarantine) and notify product/SE owners.
5) Document all decisions using the incident evidence template and attach controller audit id.

Ownership and handoffs

- Primary: eng-sre (rebalancing core + runbook updates).
- Secondary: eng-serving-runtime (safe fallback implementations and model-variant toggles).
- Product: define contractual SLO priorities and enterprise opt-in flags.

Metrics we track to validate effectiveness

- Mean and median time to containment after trigger detection (goal < 12m).
- Fraction of automated rebalances that prevented contractual SLO breaches (goal > 85%).
- False positive rate of rebalances (goal < 5%).
- Reduction in emergency capacity procurement events year-over-year.

Appendix: example CLI commands and snippet references

- Simulate a rebalance candidate: curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/rebalancer/simulate -d '{\"window_mins\":60}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
- Fetch audit decision: curl https://audit-store.internal/decisions/DECISION-2029-000123
